item.title: Making sense of Fresno State’s bowl possibilities
item.description: SAN MARCOS, TX - NOVEMBER 14: Fresno State Bulldogs RB Rayshon Luke (2) gets chased by Texas State Bobcats LB Terrence Cooks II (16) during game featuring the Fresno State Bulldogs and the Texas State Bobcats on November 14, 2026 at UFCU Stadium in San Marcos, TX. (Photo by John Rivera/Icon Sportswire via Getty Images) | Icon Sportswire via Getty Images Following a 37-35 loss to the Texas State Bobcats over the weekend, the Fresno State Bulldogs sit at 5-5 overall and 2-4 in the Pac-12 with two games to go, needing to win one of the final two to even become bowl eligible in what has turned into a disappointing season. However, with the aforementioned sixth win, the Bulldogs can end on some positive notes. A bowl game would be somewhat positive in that for the first two seasons under Matt Entz the Bulldogs would’ve made a bowl game. It would appear as though Boise State will represent the Group of Six for the College Football Playoffs, following New Mexico’s loss to UNLV on Saturday night, meaning that the position in the Poinsettia Bowl would open up. Right now, this appears to be the likely landing spot if the Bulldogs can become bowl eligible. Although another win by Texas State could make it very interesting for Fresno State when coming to bowl selection. ESPN Events runs another set of four bowls that could take potentially bowl eligible Pac-12 teams. The difficulty is that there are only two current bowl eligible teams from the conference with Boise State and Texas State being the only two. Fresno State, Oregon State and San Diego State sit one win away. Utah State is the only other school that can make six wins as they sit at 4-6 this year. Oregon State and Utah State play each other this upcoming weekend, meaning that if Utah State loses, then they are eliminated from bowl contention. San Diego State plays at Boise State and then ends the year with a likely matchup with Fresno State. And lastly, the Bulldogs take on a lowly Colorado State team this weekend needing that all important last win. A nightmare scenario is if Fresno State is stunned by Colorado State, much in the same way they were last season, and then lose to San Diego State on Thanksgiving weekend. Another nightmare scenario is if Boise State drops one of their two contests and pulls another Group of Six team back into the fold for the CFP. If Boise State somehow drops out of the CFP, then the trickle-down effect would likely land Fresno State even lower on the pecking order to the First Responder Bowl or the Gasparilla Bowl. Although it would seem more beneficial for everyone involved if Fresno State stayed closer to home like last year when they were in the Arizona Bowl. If that is the case, not only is the Poinsettia Bowl likely, but also perhaps the Famous Idaho Potato Bowl. The Hawaii Bowl and the Armed Forces Bowl also appear to be likely landing spots for Fresno State. item.description: SACRAMENTO, CA — Keegan Murray drilled a 3-pointer during the third quarter, signaling the start of a traditional celebration inside Golden 1 Center. "Keeeeegan," the public address announcer hollered. "Muuuuurray," the Sacramento Kings crowd chanted back. But the celebration didn't last long. It ended on the very next play, as Shai Gilgeous-Alexander shook his defender with a stepback before connecting on a triple of his own. That silenced everyone inside the arena. There's no better feeling when on the road. And it must've hit even harder for Gilgeous-Alexander and the OKC Thunder , who've been surrounded by a lot of outside noise lately. OKC entered Sunday's game against Sacramento on a three-game skid. And while some of that could be overlooked due to the fact that it's short-handed, there was no excusing its recent loss to the struggling Los Angeles Clippers . But OKC got back on track with a 125-103 win . A much-needed victory to finish a four-game road trip, which is the longest road trip of the season for the Thunder (9-5). Gilgeous-Alexander led OKC with 37 points, two assists and two rebounds in just 29 minutes on 13-for-20 shooting from the field (4 for 5 from deep). Aday Mara also recorded 16 points, 13 rebounds and three assists in 25 minutes on 8-for-11 shooting from the field. Here are three takeaways from the win: More: Inside Ty Jerome's rise from OKC Thunder reserve to face of Memphis Grizzlies basketball Ajay Mitchell hit the ground running in his return from ankle injury Ajay Mitchell looked just fine when he walked onto the Golden 1 Center floor on Sunday night. There was no hitch in his stride after missing the last two games due to a sprained left ankle. And when the ball tipped up, there was nothing that kept him from hitting the ground running either. Mitchell came out of the gates hot by hitting a triple for OKC's first points of the night. Then he showcased his mid-range game by sinking a 10-foot floater. Then he flashed his facilitating skills by finding Gilgeous-Alexander for an easy bucket. Then he displayed his defensive skills by intercepting a pass. It only took five minutes of game time for Mitchell to show just how valuable he is to OKC. The 24-year-old guard does it all, and it was all missed during his brief absence. item.description: BLACKSBURG, VIRGINIA - OCTOBER 17: Head coach James Franklin of the Virginia Tech Hokies reacts after a touchdown against the Georgia Tech Yellow Jackets during the third quarter at Lane Stadium on October 17, 2026 in Blacksburg, Virginia. (Photo by Michael Shroyer/Getty Images) | Getty Images The Virginia Tech Hokies had what many believed was a season-defining win over the Clemson Tigers in Death Valley three weeks ago. Since then, the Hokies have had a bye week and two ugly blowout losses. On Saturday night, Virginia Tech suffered one of the most embarrassing, inexplicable losses in school history, falling 40-22 to Stanford. You could make the case that the ODU loss that got Brent Pry fired was worse, or that horrific Friday night loss to Duke under Justin Fuente, but considering everyone’s overall optimism with the program under James Franklin, this feels worse. Now that we’ve started with that, here are six takeaways from Saturday night’s disaster. Players looked disinterested Tell me I’m wrong. I don’t care. That entire defense acted like it was too cold last night and they would’ve rather been anywhere else. Yet they were facing a team from California, which isn’t used to playing in cold weather. Yet, the team that flew across the country and hadn’t won a road game in two years looked much more comfortable. How is that possible? In our preview, we shared Stanford’s offensive and defensive rankings. The Cardinal were bad — like really bad. You can always tell a player’s effort by how they tackle. Well, no one on Virginia Tech’s roster was interested in tackling on Saturday night. With no disrespect meant to Davis Warren, Micah Ford and Benji Blackburn, they aren’t Andrew Luck, Christian McCaffrey, or Zach Ertz. The Hokies made them all look like that and more. Ford probably broke 77 tackles on 27 carries. A bad look for Virginia Tech’s players in front of another sold-out crowd that came to support them. item.title: Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers’ fading powers highlighted by stunning SNF stat vs. Bengals
item.description: Ken Blaze-Imagn Images Steelers QB Aaron Rodgers’ fading powers highlighted by stunning SNF stat vs. Bengals appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . Aaron Rodgers is old now. At 42 years old, the Steelers quarterback is no longer the MVP-winning superstar in his prime. Rodgers’ performance to start Sunday Night Football against the Cincinnati Bengals is another perfect illustration of how much Rodgers’ star has faded. Rodgers went 0-of-7 to start the game against the Bengals, which, per ESPN Insights, is the most passes he’s thrown without a completion to start a game in his illustrious 22-year career. His previous high before Sunday night was a mere four straight incompletions. Rodgers eventually did complete a pass, but he went just 4-of-12 for 25 yards in the first half. On the other side, Bengals QB Joe Burrow was busy putting up vintage Rodgers numbers, going 26-of-34 for 302 yards with three touchdown passes to give the Bengals a commanding 24-3 lead. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Amid a 6-2 start to the season, Rodgers has been the clear weak link in the Steelers’ chain. He’s completing a career-worst 60.8% of his passes for 1,871 yards with 13 touchdowns and six interceptions. That’s just the sad reality of aging. Rodgers should be commended for still being a somewhat competent starting NFL quarterback in his early 40s. But not even an all-time great like him can ward off Father Time like Tom Brady seemingly did after playing until he was 45 . For the Steelers, they will have to come to grips with Rodgers’ limitations if they are to remain successful this season. They need to continue to rely on the combination of defense and the running game to keep the wins coming. item.description: ARLINGTON, Texas — Earlier this week, Keenan Allen said his head was spinning. Acquired at the trade deadline from the Colts, it was his job to get up to speed on Kyle Shanahan’s complex and extensive playbook in time to make an impact in just a few days’ time. After making his debut in the 49ers’ 46-40 win over the Cowboys on Sunday? “It wasn’t too bad,” Allen smiled. “Wasn’t too bad. Not too bad.” Sounds like a guy who’s head is firmly on straight. San Francisco 49ers wide receiver Keenan Allen reacts after a catch against the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium in Arlington, Texas, Sunday, Nov. 15, 2026. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Allen looked the part for the better part of the preceding three hours. Five days after he touched down in Santa Clara, Allen caught more from Brock Purdy than anybody besides George Kittle. “We were just playing ball,” the 34-year-old veteran said after his first game with his fourth team. The final tally: Seven targets, five catches, 61 yards. Kittle hauled in one more pass for an additional 13 yards, and Christian McCaffrey outgained both of them with touchdown scampers of 66 and 74 yards, respectively. item.description: Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback Aaron Rodgers was replaced by backup Mason Rudolph during the fourth quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 game against the Cincinnati Bengals at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football , with the Steelers trailing 38-11. Rodgers had 143 passing yards with two touchdowns, mostly in garbage time. He was sacked three times. Rodgers' announcement in May that he'll retire after the 2026 season means the Bengals may not face the future Pro Football Hall of Famer again. Joe Flacco replaced Joe Burrow at QB for the Bengals earlier in the fourth quarter. The Bengals lost to the Steelers at Pittsburgh's Acrisure Stadium in NFL Week 3 on Sunday, Sept. 27. Rodgers, who is in his 22nd NFL season, passed for 292 yards and three touchdowns, with one interception. Rodgers and the Bengals' Joe Flacco are the NFL's oldest active quarterbacks. Rodgers turned 42 years old last December. Flacco turned 41 in January. In 2025, a Week 7 Steelers-Bengals meeting at Paycor Stadium, Flacco and Cincinnati prevailed, 33-31 , in a game the Steelers' Cam Heyward dubbed the " Icy Hot Bowl ." Rodgers and the Steelers avenged the loss four weeks later in Pittsburgh, though Rodgers was replaced after suffering a left wrist injury in the second quarter. Rodgers is 4-3 against the Bengals in 20 NFL seasons. Rodgers' first four career games against the Bengals took place while he quarterbacked the Green Bay Packers , before he split his two meetings with Cincinnati last season and defeated the Bengals earlier this season. When Andy Dalton and the Bengals visited Lambeau Field in September 2017 , they led 21-7 at the half. But the Packers rallied to outscore Cincinnati 17-3 in the second half and beat the Bengals on a Mason Crosby field goal at the end of overtime. Rodgers passed for 313 yards with three touchdowns in that game. Rodgers' 2021 matchup with Joe Burrow ended in heartbreak for the Bengals. item.description: The Phoenix gym has steadily grown its reputation as a centre of boxing excellence [Boxxer] In the red corner, a two-time world champion staying sharp as he waits for his return. His opponents, a succession of boxers readying themselves for an undercard bout that could be a key step in their careers. And out the back, the fancy dress climax to a Halloween boxing camp for local kids that mixed the sweet science with arts and crafts. Welcome to Llanrumney Phoenix ABC, situated on the eastern edge of Cardiff as the suburbs rise up and away from the city centre of the Welsh capital. Barrett stops Gwynne for vacant lightweight title Adames beats Welshman Warburton by unanimous decision Cordina unlikely to fight Pacquiao on Joshua-Fury card It is both six kilometres and a million miles away from the bright lights of the Principality Stadium, the focus of the boxing world on 11 December when it stages the heavyweight showdown between Anthony Joshua and Tyson Fury. But it is also the place where the steps towards it are made. Some are further along than others, such as Joe Cordina, whose image complete with world title straps is one of several champions that hang high above the main sparring ring, flanked by a plethora of punchbags. Or former featherweight champ Lee Selby, now a bareknuckle boxer but lending his experience to the sparring as Gavin Gwynne gets ready for his own battle with Zelfa Barrett, a bout that would ultimately end in a fifth-round stoppage for the Welshman. item.description: Defensive coordinator Christian Parker of the Dallas Cowboys Getty Give the Dallas Cowboys some credit. The loss to the 49ers on Sunday in Week 10 looked a lot more like the way the Cowboys were supposed to look this season, with a high-powered offense that could keep up with anybody and a defense that just maybe showed enough improvement for Dak Prescott and Co. to be able to keep their heads above water in most games. The win against the Texans in Week 4 was a good example, and the Week 10 showing against the 49ers certainly had the potential to be much the same. Except that the Cowboys defense could not make enough plays, and one decision in particular–to somehow leave Von Miller at age 37, in coverage on star running back Christian McCaffrey in the fourth quarter–stood out as a major blunder for coordinator Christian Parker. The play took place with just 3:23 to go in the game and the Cowboys having cut the lead to 38-32. Brock Purdy found McCaffrey in the flat with Miller–either intentionally or in a mix-up–in coverage, and the mismatch was easily exploited. McCaffrey bolted for a 66-yard touchdown all but untouched, en route to the 46-40 win. It was not a game whose film Parker–already beleaguered because of the Cowboys’ inability to show consistent progress–will likely treasure. The Cowboys set a record for yardage allowed at home, giving up 584 yards to the 49ers, who seemed to get only occasional resistance from Dallas. And again, fair or not, Parker took the hit for that dreadful McCaffrey touchdown. item.description: The San Francisco 49ers traveled south to take on the Dallas Cowboys at AT&T Stadium on Sunday for a battle between non-division NFC rivals, and Kyle Shanahan's team earned a 46-40 win, moving to 8-1 on the year. item.title: Are 49ers due for a reality check? Red flags emerged in wild win over Cowboys
item.description: San Francisco 49ers quarterback Brock Purdy, bottom, is sacked by Dallas Cowboys defensive tackle LT Overton during the first half on Sunday in Arlington, Texas. (Tony Gutierrez/Associated Press) The San Francisco 49ers second travelogue trip of the season got off to an exciting start on Sunday, surviving a wild - and somewhat alarming - shootout with the Dallas Cowboys, 46-40. Now they head from the plains of Texas to the Rocky Mountains and then take a hard left to go south of the border to Mexico City, during their second lengthy, multi-country trip. The good news is the 49ers are tied for a league best 8-1. The better news - for the coaches - is that, during this long week away from home, the 49ers have plenty to keep them occupied. Like tightening up that problematic defense. Improving the pass rush. And keeping Brock Purdy upright. Twelve days after Democrats turned Texas blue, 49ers fans turned Dallas red, taking over AT&T Stadium and making Jerry Jones' palace sound like their home stadium. For the fans' next trick, they'll try to turn Mexico red. "Our fans are awesome," head coach Kyle Shanahan said. "Wish I could give them all game balls." The 49ers have cruised to an 8-1 record, and the most impressive part of the first half of the season has been vanquishing their most heated rivals away from their home stadium: the Rams in Australia, the Seahawks in Seattle and, on Sunday, the Cowboys, in Arlington, Texas. But the upcoming second half of the season holds some potential concerns. And Sunday's split personality game underscored those worries. "It was sort of a weird game," Purdy said. While the 49ers offense looked like the most elite on the planet on Sunday, racking up 584 yards, the 49ers defense couldn't say the same thing. The 49ers swamped the Cowboys from the end of the second quarter until early in the fourth quarter, outscoring Dallas 28-3 in that stretch. But then the 49ers found themselves in an uncomfortably tight situation, giving up three Dallas touchdowns in the final 9:08 of the game and having to survive an onside kick, their own fumble (that they recovered), a three-and-out and a Dallas attempt at a Cal Bears-style lateral-fest comeback. "Anytime you get 40 dropped on you, you're going to be upset," said linebacker Fred Warner . "You've got to look at the tape and see why that was the case." There will be a lot of tape to watch in the coming week, while getting acclimated to altitude in Colorado Springs. Though the first half of the season has gone almost perfectly, there is still a long road ahead. Next week, in Estadio Azteca, the 49ers will face Minnesota, a team that - unlike the Cowboys - will present a ferocious defense. And, with the addition of Kirk Cousins, a team that suddenly looks like a true Super Bowl contender. item.title: Joe Flacco replaces Joe Burrow in 4th quarter of Bengals-Steelers rout
item.description: Cincinnati Bengals backup quarterback Joe Flacco entered in the fourth quarter of the team's NFL Week 10 game against the Pittsburgh Steelers at Paycor Stadium on NBC's Sunday Night Football , as the Bengals sat starter Joe Burrow with a 38-18 lead. Burrow left the game having completed 35-of-44 for 409 passing yards with four touchdowns. He had 302 passing yards in the first half . When Flacco started for the Bengals in 2025 against Aaron Rodgers, ESPN Research reported that it was the second time in NFL history that two quarterbacks at least 40 years old face off in a regular-season or postseason game. The Steelers' Cam Heyward dubbed it the "Icy Hot" Bowl . Rodgers is the only active NFL quarterback older than Flacco. Rodgers' announcement in May that he'll retire after the 2026 season means the Bengals may not face the future Pro Football Hall of Famer again. Flacco got to enter the team's NFL Week 7 rout of the Ravens in Baltimore during the fourth quarter and finish the game against his former team, but he did not attempt a pass. Flacco entered Week 7 having appeared in one game for the Bengals this season but without attempting a pass. Flacco told Burrow he thought Burrow's first touchdown pass to Ja'Marr Chase against the Houston Texans was "uncatchable." Rodgers' announcement in May that he'll retire after the 2026 season means the Bengals may not face the future Pro Football Hall of Famer again. Flacco, who turned 41 in January, played in nine games last season for the Bengals , making six starts after Burrow suffered a turf toe injury during a Week 2 win against Jacksonville . Flacco completed 158 of 254 pass attempts for 1,664 yards with 13 touchdowns. In November 2025, Flacco played with a sprained AC joint in his throwing shoulder during a 47-42 loss to the Chicago Bears . At 40 years old, Flacco became the oldest quarterback in NFL history to pass for 470 yards in a game. item.title: St. John’s men’s basketball squeezes Syracuse behind second half defensive display
item.description: Nov 15, 2026; New York, New York, USA; St. John's Red Storm forward Keyshawn Hall (7) celebrates in the second half against the Syracuse Orange at Madison Square Garden. Mandatory Credit: Wendell Cruz-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect The entire first half of Sunday’s game was tailor-made to get on the nerves of St. John’s, whether it was Ryan Moesch dropped Ruben Prey with a crossover in cinematic fashion before sinking a three, the 11-2 run by the visitors fueled by careless Red Storm turnovers, or the thousands of traveling Syracuse fans making Madison Square Garden feel like the Carrier Dome JMA Wireless Dome as they watched their underdog Orange enter the halftime with the lead despite giving up 13 first-half turnovers. St. John’s could have lost their composure and let an upset bid become a reality, but they responded like a contender should in their first brush with adversity this season, flipping momentum with a suffocating lockdown performance in the second half to seal a 79-62 win and improve to 4-0. After allowing Syracuse to shoot 58.3% in the first half, Red Storm made the right adjustments and shut down the Orange’s offense after the break, sealing the paint and forcing ill-advised shots from the outside. Syracuse shot 11-of-33 in the second half and went 3-of-14 from deep. The Johnnies forced a season-high 21 turnovers over both halves, including nine by Ryan Moesch, and cashed in 32 points off those takeaways. The Red Storm allowed a Sadiq White, Jr. layup out of the break, then went on a 16-0 run over the following seven minutes to take control with a 46-35 lead. Keyshawn Hall punctuated this spurt with a pull-up triple and he would finish the night with 18 points (8-of-18 from the field), a dozen of those points coming in the second half. KEYSHAWN TRIPLE pic.twitter.com/6nXvS9mUYi — St. John's Men’s Basketball (@StJohnsBBall) November 16, 2026 Syracuse later made one final run to cut the Red Storm lead down to seven points with 2:52 left, but the Red Storm salted away the win with clutch free throws and fastbreak buckets off after breaking the Orange’s press. Including Hall, all five Red Storm starters finished the night in double figures. Tounde Yessoufou led the Johnnies with a 19-point, 14-rebound double-double, the second of his college career and his first in a St. John’s uniform. Sunday’s victory marks the fifth consecutive time St. John’s has defeated Syracuse, their longest winning streak in the series history since 1969-70. Tounde slam gets @TheGarden ROCKING 🔴⛈️ pic.twitter.com/xdE0tqzsPY — St. John's Men’s Basketball (@StJohnsBBall) November 16, 2026 Before they head westward for the Players Era Festival, St. John’s will take on Gerry McNamara’s former team, Siena, in their last tune-up on Wednesday, November 18. Tip-off from Carnesecca Arena is scheduled for 7:00 p.m. For fans eager to finally see the Red Storm on television this year, the game will air on truTV.
